report_name: Unit 42 Details First Ransomware Attack Using Autonomous AI Agents

threat_actors.name: Unnamed AI-Assisted Attacker
threat_actors.description: A threat actor who utilized frontier AI models and autonomous agentic frameworks to execute a rapid ransomware attack, compressing weeks of activity into less than ten hours.

attack_patterns.name: Network Service Discovery
attack_patterns.description: Autonomous AI agents mapped the internal network architecture to identify key assets as part of the initial reconnaissance phase.

attack_patterns.name: System Information Discovery
attack_patterns.description: Autonomous AI agents likely gathered system information to understand operating systems and configurations on the victim network.

attack_patterns.name: Remote System Discovery
attack_patterns.description: Autonomous AI agents likely performed remote system discovery to map out the internal network topology.

attack_patterns.name: OS Credential Dumping
attack_patterns.description: Autonomous AI agents located and seized root credentials from compromised hosts on the network.

attack_patterns.name: Unsecured Credentials
attack_patterns.description: Autonomous AI agents located and seized master keys for the victim's cloud AI infrastructure.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Cloud Storage
attack_patterns.description: Autonomous AI agents accessed and exfiltrated data from source code repositories, which were likely hosted in cloud storage.

attack_patterns.name: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
attack_patterns.description: Autonomous AI agents triggered unauthorized builds within the Continuous Integration/Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) pipeline to further their objectives.

attack_patterns.name: Acquire Public AI Artifacts
attack_patterns.description: The report confirms the use of AI systems to perform discovery tasks, referencing this MITRE ATLAS technique.

attack_patterns.name: Deploy AI Agent
attack_patterns.description: The attacker deployed multiple autonomous AI agents into the victim environment after gaining initial access to carry out the attack.

attack_patterns.name: Internal Defacement
attack_patterns.description: The attacker left behind an 80-page, technically detailed audit of the victim's security flaws, likely generated by the AI agents, as a psychological tool and demonstration of capability.

tools.name: Autonomous AI Agent Framework
tools.description: A framework leveraging frontier AI models to deploy autonomous agents capable of performing coordinated attack actions like reconnaissance, exfiltration, and infrastructure compromise.

infrastructure.name: Compromised CI/CD Pipeline
infrastructure.description: The victim's CI/CD pipeline was compromised and used by AI agents to trigger unauthorized builds for execution and potential persistence.

indicators.name: AI-Assisted Rapid Discovery Commands
indicators.pattern:
title: AI-Assisted Rapid Discovery Commands
id: 7f8b1e2a-9c3d-4f5a-8b1c-2d3e4f5a6b7c
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects the execution of common discovery commands. A rapid succession of these commands from a single host or user context in a short time frame may indicate automated reconnaissance by an AI agent.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/ai-assisted-cyber-attack-inside-a-unit-42-investigation/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-02
tags:
  - attack.t1082
  - attack.t1018
  - attack.t1046
  - attack.discovery
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_whoami:
    Image|endswith: '\whoami.exe'
  selection_net:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\net.exe'
      - '\net1.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: ' user'
  selection_ipconfig:
    Image|endswith: '\ipconfig.exe'
  selection_arp:
    Image|endswith: '\arp.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: ' -a'
  condition: 1 of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate administrative activity.
  - Diagnostic scripts.
indicators.description: Detects a pattern of rapid discovery commands (whoami, net user, ipconfig, arp -a) from a single host, which is indicative of machine-speed reconnaissance performed by AI agents.

indicators.name: Anomalous Cloud IAM Credential Management
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Cloud IAM Credential Management
id: 3a4b5c6d-7e8f-4a9b-8c1d-2e3f4a5b6c7d
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects anomalous usage of cloud management APIs for credential creation or modification. This may indicate compromise by an AI agent attempting to seize control of cloud infrastructure by creating or modifying access keys and user roles.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/ai-assisted-cyber-attack-inside-a-unit-42-investigation/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-02
tags:
  - attack.t1552
  - attack.credential_access
level: high
logsource:
  product: aws
  service: cloudtrail
detection:
  selection:
    eventSource: 'iam.amazonaws.com'
    eventName:
      - 'CreateAccessKey'
      - 'CreateLoginProfile'
      - 'UpdateAccessKey'
      - 'CreateUser'
      - 'AddUserToGroup'
      - 'PutUserPolicy'
      - 'AttachUserPolicy'
  filter_known_automation:
    userIdentity.arn|contains:
      - 'role/KnownAdminRole'
      - 'role/CICD-Runner'
  condition: selection and not filter_known_automation
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate administrative actions for user and access key management.
indicators.description: Detects anomalous usage of cloud management APIs, especially for credential creation or modification, from unfamiliar sources, suggesting an AI agent is attempting to seize master keys.
